Geng, forcing himself despite illness, asked that selection be entrusted to court recommendation; Yu Shenxing, Li Tingji, and Ye Xianggao were appointed, and Wang Xijue was recalled from home as chief secretary. Supervising Secretaries Wang Yuanhan and Hu Xin, saying Tingji's appointment was Geng's doing, denounced Tingji and attacked Geng. Geng declined; the emperor sharply rebuked the censorate. Jiang Shichang and Song Tao were then demoted; the censorate believed this came from Geng and grew more resentful. Rites Director Zheng Zhenxian impeached Geng on twelve major counts and said Geng with Yiguan and Xijue formed the three bodies of past, present, and future. The emperor demoted Zhenxian three ranks; when censorate officials pleaded for him he was demoted two ranks more.

sentences.zh: 先，考選科道，吏部擬上七十八人．候命踰年，不下，賡連疏趣之．三十六年秋，命始下．諸人列言路，方欲見風采，而給事中若霖先嘗忤賡，及是見黜，適當賡病起入直時．謂賡修郤，攻訐四起，先後疏論至五十餘人．給事中喻安性者，賡里人，為賡上疏言：「今日政權不由內閣，盡移於司禮．」言者遂交章劾安性，復侵賡．是時賡已寢疾，乞休疏二十餘上．言者慮其復起，攻不已，而賡以十一月卒於官．遺疏陳時政，語極悲切．賡先加少保兼太子太保，進吏部尚書、文華殿大學士．及卒，贈太保，諡文懿．御史彭端吾復疏詆賡，給事中胡忻請停其贈諡，帝不聽．

translations.literal: Earlier, in the selection examination for censorate officials, the Ministry of Personnel proposed seventy-eight men. They waited for orders more than a year without response; Geng submitted successive memorials urging action. In the autumn of the thirty-sixth year the orders at last came down. The men took their places in the remonstrance offices and were just about to show their mettle when Supervising Secretary Ruolin, who had earlier offended Geng, was dismissed just as Geng was rising from illness to attend duty. They believed Geng was settling old scores; attacks and denunciations erupted on every side, and in succession more than fifty memorials criticized him. Supervising Secretary Yu Anxing, a townsman of Geng, submitted a memorial for Geng saying: 'Today governmental power does not lie with the Grand Secretariat but has entirely shifted to the Directorate of Ceremonial.' Remonstrance officials thereupon submitted successive memorials impeaching Anxing and again attacking Geng. By this time Geng was already bedridden; more than twenty memorials asking to retire had been submitted. Remonstrance officials feared he would rise again and attacked without cease, while Geng died in office in the eleventh month. His final memorial set forth current policy in language of utmost grief. Geng had earlier been given the additional ranks of Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince and promoted to Minister of Personnel and Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall. When he died he was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Wenyi. Censor Peng Duanwu again submitted a memorial denouncing Geng; Supervising Secretary Hu Xin asked that his posthumous honors be halted; the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the censorate selection examination the Ministry of Personnel proposed seventy-eight men. They waited more than a year for orders; Geng submitted successive memorials urging action. In the autumn of the thirty-sixth year the orders came down. The men took their places in the censorate and were just about to show their mettle when Supervising Secretary Ruolin, who had earlier offended Geng, was dismissed just as Geng was rising from illness to attend duty. They believed Geng was settling old scores; attacks erupted on every side, and more than fifty memorials criticized him in succession. Supervising Secretary Yu Anxing, Geng's townsman, submitted a memorial for him saying: 'Today governmental power does not lie with the Grand Secretariat but has entirely shifted to the Directorate of Ceremonial.' Censorate officials then impeached Anxing in succession and again attacked Geng. By then Geng was bedridden; he had submitted more than twenty retirement memorials. Censorate officials feared he would rise again and attacked without cease, while Geng died in office in the eleventh month. His final memorial on current policy was utterly grief-stricken. He had earlier been made Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince and promoted to Minister of Personnel and Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall. When he died he was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Wenyi. Censor Peng Duanwu again denounced him; Supervising Secretary Hu Xin asked that his posthumous honors be halted; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 賡醇謹無大過，與沈一貫同鄉相比，暱給事中陳治則、姚文蔚等，以故蒙詬病云．

translations.literal: Geng was sober and cautious without major faults, but being from the same district as Shen Yiguan he associated closely with him and was intimate with Supervising Secretaries Chen Zhize, Yao Wenwei, and others; for this reason he suffered reproach and criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Geng was sober and cautious without major faults, but as a townsman of Shen Yiguan he associated closely with him and was intimate with Supervising Secretaries Chen Zhize, Yao Wenwei, and others; for this he suffered reproach.

sentences.zh: 朱敬循

translations.literal: Zhu Jingxun
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jingxun

sentences.zh: 子敬循，官禮部郎中，改稽勳．前此無正郎改吏部者，自敬循始．終右通政．

translations.literal: His son Jingxun served as Director in the Ministry of Rites and transferred to Records of Merit. Before this no regular director had transferred to the Ministry of Personnel; Jingxun was the first. He ended as Right Vice Commissioner of Communications.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingxun served as a director in the Ministry of Rites and transferred to Records of Merit—the first regular director to move to the Ministry of Personnel. He ended as Right Vice Commissioner of Communications.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：四維等當軸處中，頗滋物議。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Siwei and the others, holding the axis and standing at the center, aroused considerable public criticism.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Siwei and the others, holding power at the center of government, aroused considerable public criticism.

sentences.zh: 其時言路勢張，恣為抨擊。

translations.literal: At that time the remonstrance offices were powerful and struck out at will.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the censorate was powerful and attacked at will.

sentences.zh: 是非瞀亂，賢否混淆，相敵仇，罔顧國是。

translations.literal: Right and wrong were confused, the worthy and unworthy were mingled, factions treated one another as enemies, and the good of the state was disregarded.
translations.idiomatic: Right and wrong were confused, the worthy and unworthy mingled, factions treated one another as enemies, and the good of the state was disregarded.

sentences.zh: 詬誶日積，又烏足為定論乎。

translations.literal: Abuse piled up day by day—how could it suffice as a final judgment?
translations.idiomatic: Abuse piled up day by day—how could any of it stand as final judgment?

sentences.zh: 然謂光明磊落有大臣之節，則斯人亦不能無愧辭焉。

translations.literal: Yet to say they were open and upright and possessed a grand minister's integrity—these men too cannot be without words of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to call them open, upright, and possessed of a grand minister's integrity—these men too cannot escape reproach.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: [一] 踰一日時行亦罷 一日，原作「一月」。

translations.literal: [1] One day later Shixing was also dismissed. One day—the original read 'one month.'
translations.idiomatic: [1] 'One day later Shixing was also dismissed.' The original text read 'one month.'

sentences.zh: 本書卷一一０宰輔年表萬曆十九年：時行「九月致仕」，國「九月致仕」。

translations.literal: In this book, Volume 110, Grand Ministers Chronological Table, Wanli nineteenth year: Shixing 'retired in the ninth month,' Guo 'retired in the ninth month.'
translations.idiomatic: Volume 110 of this work, Grand Ministers Chronological Table, Wanli year 19: Shixing 'retired in the ninth month,' Guo 'retired in the ninth month.'

sentences.zh: 兩人致仕都在九月。

translations.literal: Both men retired in the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: Both men retired in the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 神宗實錄卷二四０萬曆十九年九月、國榷卷七五頁四六五八都作壬申許國去，甲戌，申時行去，正踰一日。

translations.literal: Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong, juan 240, ninth month of Wanli nineteenth year, and Guoque juan 75, page 4658, both read: on renshen Xu Guo left; on jiaxu Shen Shixing left—exactly one day apart.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong, juan 240, ninth month of Wanli 19, and Guoque juan 75, page 4658, both read: on renshen Xu Guo left; on jiaxu Shen Shixing left—exactly one day apart.

sentences.zh: 據改。

translations.literal: Amended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Amended accordingly.

sentences.zh: [二] 用給事中馮景隆御史孫維城薦 孫維城，原作「孫惟成」，據神宗實錄卷一三三萬曆十一年丙戌條、明進士題名碑錄隆慶辛未科改。

translations.literal: [2] On recommendation of Supervising Secretary Feng Jinglong and Censor Sun Weicheng. Sun Weicheng—the original read 'Sun Weicheng'; amended according to Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong, juan 133, entry for bingxu of Wanli eleventh year, and the Stele Record of Ming Jinshi, Longqing xinwei cohort.
translations.idiomatic: [2] 'On recommendation of Supervising Secretary Feng Jinglong and Censor Sun Weicheng.' Sun Weicheng—the original read 'Sun Weicheng'; amended according to the Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong, juan 133, Wanli 11 bingxu entry, and the Stele Record of Ming Jinshi, Longqing xinwei cohort.
